learningObjective: Set up Azure-to-Azure replication with Site Recovery, run test failovers, fail over to a second region, commit, re-protect and fail back.
engineer: Where the vault goes: create the Recovery Services vault in the target region, not the source region.

Turning on replication: from the VM (Disaster recovery) or from the vault. Choose the target region; the resource group; the VNet and subnet; availability options; a cache storage account in the source region; a replication policy. The Mobility service extension is installed on the VMs.
Replication policy: keeps recovery points for up to 15 days, and sets how often app-consistent snapshots are taken.
Network mapping: says which target VNet each source VNet fails over to.
Recovery plans: put VMs into ordered groups, with scripts or manual steps in between, for apps with several tiers.
Test failover: pick a recovery point and an isolated VNet. Check the app works. Then click Cleanup test failover. Production isn't touched.
Recovery point choices: Latest, the least data lost, but slower because it processes pending data first; Latest processed, the fastest recovery; Latest app-consistent; Custom.
After a real failover: Commit, which throws away the other recovery points; Re-protect, which starts copying from the second region back to the first; later, fail back the same way.
RPO and RTO: RPO is how much data you can afford to lose. RTO is how long recovery can take. Site Recovery copies continuously, so RPO for Azure VMs is low.

example.title: A disaster recovery drill every quarter
body: Every quarter, the team runs a test failover of the recovery plan 'erp' into vnet-dr-test in West US. They run quick tests, then clean up.
During a real East US outage, they failed over with Latest processed and committed. When East US came back, they re-protected, and failed back a week later.

architectureDecisions: Apps with several tiers: use recovery plans, so VMs start in the right order.
Test regularly: run test failovers every quarter and after big changes.
Pick the recovery point on purpose: Latest processed for the fastest recovery, Latest for the least data lost.

comparisons.difference: Restores from backups, so more data lost and slower recovery. Site Recovery copies all the time.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't pick a vault in the source region.
troubleshooting.cause: For Azure-to-Azure, the vault must be in another region.
troubleshooting.fix: Create the vault in the target region.

troubleshooting.symptom: VMs can't reach each other after failover.
troubleshooting.cause: No network mapping, or the wrong subnet.
troubleshooting.fix: Set up network mapping, and check the recovery plan order.

configuration.limits: Recovery points kept up to 15 days
The vault must be in a different region from the source
configuration.permissions: Site Recovery Contributor on the vault, plus Virtual Machine Contributor in the source and target
